chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who had a debt owed to me, and he was absent from me for a period. Then I saw him circumambulating around the Ka'bah, so I went to collect the debt from him. He said: 'Do not greet him, and do not startle him until he exits the Haram (sanctuary).'

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The sanctuary, specifically referring to the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) in Mecca.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cubic building at the center of the Grand Mosque in Mecca.
key_terms.يَتَقَاضَاهُ: To collect a debt from someone.
key_terms.يَطُوفُ: Circumambulating, performing tawaf around the Ka'bah.

ai.seo_question: How should a creditor approach a debtor who is performing tawaf at the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a balance between the creditor's right to collect and the sanctity of the ritual state by instructing the creditor to wait until the debtor exits the Haram boundaries. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of preserving the dignity and concentration (khushu') of the worshipper, ensuring that the debt collection does not invalidate or disturb the tawaf. It highlights the practical application of respecting sacred spaces while enforcing financial obligations.
